name: Virology
boundaries: Virology: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.original_title: Definitive pre-cellular origin of viruses and divergence of a fixed six realms
original_dispositions.reason: ICTV realm taxonomy is already in use and is being split. Finishing the historical reconstruction would deepen an existing framework but would not, by itself, create a capability beyond VIR-01 and VIR-08. The “six realms” count is already outdated.

original_dispositions.original_title: One conserved target for a drug active against all RNA and DNA viruses
original_dispositions.reason: The formulary is the capability the reviews support. A literal universal molecule remains an optional, stronger way to meet the same bar.
Latency circuitry, reactivation, permanent silencing, and reservoir clearance are treated as the same missing capability.

original_dispositions.original_title: Predictive model of host-jumping and pandemic emergence
original_dispositions.reason: The prospective sequence-to-phenotype concept includes host-jump prediction.

original_dispositions.original_title: Causal mechanisms from persistent viruses to chronic disease
original_dispositions.reason: Narrowed to an interruptible chain, with EBV and multiple sclerosis as the demonstration case. Classic viral cancers and hepatitis C cure are treated as already achieved and are not re-listed.

original_dispositions.original_title: Full functional atlas and ecological roles of the global virome
original_dispositions.reason: The atlas is the product of reading function plus sampling. A particle-by-particle census is not a separate principle.

original_dispositions.original_title: Programmable safe synthetic virus for gene delivery or oncolytic therapy
original_dispositions.reason: The delivery half is covered by VIR-07. A general metastatic-cancer cure by replicating oncolytic viruses was not added; a 2025 Lancet review judged that clinical translation has lagged the early promise.

original_dispositions.original_title: Master network of endogenous viruses shaping eukaryotic complexity, placentation, and immunity
original_dispositions.reason: Endogenous viral contributions to mammalian biology are already an established research field. The historical wording does not identify a remaining capability beyond that field, and it overlaps the origin question disposed under item 1.

original_dispositions.original_title: A reproducible directed-evolution and attenuation platform
original_dispositions.reason: Directed evolution is an existing laboratory method. The resistance-proof phage outcome is part of VIR-06. Rapid vaccines are part of VIR-04 and VIR-09. The item bundles those outcomes and does not state an additional principle.

original_dispositions.original_title: A fundamentally new class of infectious agents
original_dispositions.reason: Prions and viroids already sit outside the classical virion. Obelisks were reported, but their impact on disease is explicitly undetermined. An unspecified further class is a hope rather than a defined missing capability.

reconciliation_change_log.change: VIR-01 through VIR-10 are preserved. None was deleted, replaced, or merged away.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The first-pass concepts are all retained.

reconciliation_change_log.change: VIR-01 was amended with the Dufloo et al. 2025 entry screen, now read from the paper PDF. Holmes et al. 2024 and Sikkema and Koopmans 2025 were added as the real reviews behind the historical “pandemic prediction” item.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Entry into human cells is often compatible and is not the main barrier.

reconciliation_change_log.change: The specific count of about 100 approved antivirals covering 10 of more than 200 pathogenic viruses was withdrawn. The entry now states explicitly that a single agent for every RNA and DNA virus would meet the bar and is not required.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The numerical claim came from one PDF retrieval and was not re-verified. The verified abstract still supports a thin arsenal against pathogen X, and reviews describe universal agents as rare.

reconciliation_change_log.change: VIR-03 now names the latency circuitry, reactivation, and permanent silencing as the same missing capability.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The historical reservoir item is covered without a second ID.

reconciliation_change_log.change: VIR-06 notes that a directed-evolution platform for non-resistant phage is a route to this capability, not a separate one.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The platform is a tool toward reliable phage therapy.

reconciliation_change_log.change: VIR-07 distinguishes cell-addressable, non-replicating delivery from a replicating oncolytic cure.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The oncolytic cure stays below the bar.

reconciliation_change_log.change: VIR-08 distinguishes experimental function-reading from a literal census of every virus particle. Holmes et al. 2024 and the February 2025 mSphere diversity estimate were added.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The census is a consequence of reading function plus sampling. The mSphere author list was not captured.

reconciliation_change_log.change: VIR-09 notes WHO’s April 2026 pathogen-family roadmaps.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: They are preparedness infrastructure, not a correlate.

EBV–multiple sclerosis is a virus-to-chronic-disease chain with epidemiological necessity, an incomplete mechanism, and no demonstrated prevention or reversal. That is a different capability from reservoir clearance and from family-breadth vaccines.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Historical framing sources were checked and not reused. The real fifty-year perspective is Holmes, Krammer, and Goodrum, Cell, 19 September 2024.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The claimed Nature Reviews Microbiology article, January 2026 Cell Host & Microbe Holmes paper, WHO agenda, and Annual Review of Virology chapter were not found. Annual Review of Virology volume 13 (2026) exists and does not match that description.
